case.title: Beyond graphite: Indonesian nickel from a Huayou plant
case.subtitle: PT Huayue Nickel Cobalt · Morowali (IMIP), Indonesia
case.question: Can Sayari show nickel from a Chinese-owned Indonesian plant reaching US battery supply chains, directly or through cathode makers in Korea, Japan or China?
case.answer: Partly. Sayari shows the plant's nickel intermediate going almost entirely to China, much of it to its own Chinese owners, and nothing nickel-based going straight to the US. It also shows Huayou precursor reaching POSCO Future M (to 2023) and POSCO cathode reaching a US cell plant (2026), but no record joins those steps to this plant.
case.why_it_matters: Most Indonesian nickel is processed in plants more than 25% Chinese-owned, which already kept it out of the US EV credit. From 2026 the PFE rules bring the same ownership question to the 45X manufacturing credit for US cell plants. A buyer that sees 'Korea' on its cathode invoice cannot see this plant at all, so the nickel's origin has to be traced, not assumed.
case.headline: The plant is clearly Chinese-led: Huayou 57% and CMOC 30%, per open sources, with a Chinese beneficial owner in Indonesia's register. Sayari shows 308 rows of nickel intermediate leaving it, mostly for China, and no nickel going to the US. The trail to US cell plants goes dark in China, where the MHP becomes precursor.
case.summary_for_non_experts: Batteries need nickel as well as graphite. In Indonesia, Chinese companies run huge plants that turn nickel ore into an intermediate called MHP (mixed hydroxide precipitate). We followed one, PT Huayue Nickel Cobalt, which is majority-owned by China's Huayou. Its MHP mostly goes to Huayou's own factories in China, which make precursor, the next step towards cathode. Sayari can show that next step reaching a Korean cathode maker and Korean cathode reaching a US cell plant, but it cannot show that this plant's nickel is inside.

steps.title: Why this plant
steps.text: PT Huayue Nickel Cobalt (HNC) was Huayou's first high-pressure acid leach (HPAL) plant in the Morowali park, where BTR's anode plant also sits. It started in Nov 2021 and makes about 60,000 t of nickel a year in MHP. Its shareholders are published by a listed co-owner, and Sayari has a record with its Indonesian tax ID. That makes it the best-documented test case.

steps.title: Eight records, one plant
steps.text: Sayari holds eight records for the plant. The main one has the tax ID and both the Morowali site and the Jakarta office. Four share that office address in Sopo Del Tower A; one of them is wrongly typed as a person. Three are name-only and kept as leads.

steps.title: The owner: Huayou, 57%
steps.text: Indonesia's beneficial-owner register, via Sayari, names two people: Chen Xuehua, with an address in Huayou's home city, and a second individual with a Taipei address whose role is unexplained (name withheld). An AEER report lists Chen Xuehua as a 6.43% shareholder of Huayou. The company stakes come from open sources: Huayou 57%, CMOC 30%, Nickel Industries 10%. Sayari's own shortest path to Huayou is a trade link through Huayou's import-export arm.

steps.title: Where the MHP goes
steps.text: The plant sent 308 rows of HS 7501.20, the code for nickel intermediates such as MHP. Of the 200 most recent rows (Aug 2024 – Aug 2026), 76 went to Huayou companies in Guangxi, Quzhou and Hong Kong and 20 to CMOC, its second shareholder. Most of the rest went to traders (IXM, Trafigura, Mercuria) and Chinese battery-materials makers (CNGR, Brunp, Jinchuan, Umicore's Jiangmen JV). Only India's Malco Energy sits outside China and the trading houses.

steps.title: US rows: valves, not nickel
steps.text: All 48 rows from the plant to the US are valves and valve parts with serial numbers, sent to ValvTechnologies in Houston and Caldera Engineering in Utah, Jan 2023 – Nov 2025. HPAL plants wear out such valves, so the rows fit repairs or returns. No MHP, nickel sulphate or matte goes straight to the US in these results.

steps.title: One step further: precursor to Korea, cathode to Indiana
steps.text: Huayou precursor companies shipped 29 rows of cathode precursor (HS 2853.90, 'nickel cobalt manganese hydroxide') to POSCO Future M, Dec 2021 – Dec 2023. Huayou's annual report confirms a long-term supply deal. Separately, POSCO Future M shipped 87 rows of cathode-coded HS 2841.90 to StarPlus Energy's cell plant in Kokomo, Indiana, May–Jul 2026.

steps.title: Where the trail goes dark
steps.text: Nothing joins the steps. Huayou's biggest MHP buyer in China shows no exports, and the precursor exporter is a different Huayou company with no visible MHP from this plant. The precursor rows end in Dec 2023, before the 2026 cathode rows, and POSCO says it is moving to China-free precursor. Free-text searches for 'Huayou' into the US return unrelated furniture and kitchenware.

red_flags.flag: Chinese parent ownership of the transit plant
red_flags.note: A Chinese beneficial owner in Indonesia's register; Huayou 57% and CMOC 30% per open sources.

red_flags.note: No nickel product goes to the US; the US rows are valves.

red_flags.flag: Recent incorporation vs. first export date
red_flags.note: No incorporation date in Sayari. First export row Mar 2021, before the Nov 2021 start-up.

red_flags.flag: Volume spike after a policy date
red_flags.note: We read 200 of 308 MHP rows and did not count volumes by month.

red_flags.flag: Shared address or officer with a flagged entity
red_flags.note: Shares a Jakarta office tower with other Chinese-linked nickel firms (Huafei, Eternal Nickel, Huaneng); none is a flagged entity. SOE flags describe neighbours.
Eight records for the plant, 13 for Huayou, two for StarPlus Energy.
Xinjiang and UFLPA sub-tier flags on the plant's records; these are network signals, not findings.

caveats: Processing nickel in Indonesia with Chinese investment is legal and common. Nothing here shows wrongdoing by any company named.
The US buyers are named because they appear in customs records; this says nothing about their compliance.
The ownership percentages come from Nickel Industries' 2023 filing and an AEER report (Feb 2025); stakes may have changed since.
HS 7501.20 covers several nickel intermediates. We treat these rows as MHP because the plant makes only MHP, but the rows do not say so.
We read 200 of the 308 MHP rows (Aug 2024 – Aug 2026). Earlier buyers may differ.
HS 2841.90 also carries some miscoded anode rows (Tesla, 2023). The StarPlus rows have no product text, so 'cathode' is our reading of the code.
Policy notes come from secondary summaries (Tax Law Center, Fastmarkets); check IRS Notice 2026-15 before relying on them.
Records checked 18 Oct 2026. Sayari merges and retires IDs.

calls.question: Which Sayari records describe the Huayue Nickel Cobalt plant?
calls.result_summary: 8 records. The main one (d36wLU72WGaWpEduWzxfNw) carries Indonesian tax ID 0867718132067000 and Jakarta office addresses in Sopo Del Tower A, floor 21. Four more trade-name records share that address (one typed as a person); three are name-only.
calls.interpretation: One plant, eight records; the tax ID anchors the main one.

calls.question: What does the main record hold?
calls.result_summary: Adds a Morowali industrial park address (Kec. Bahodopi). 53 ships_to and 141 receives_from partners, 2 beneficial owners. 384 shipments sent, 24,793 received. Sources: Korean, Japanese, UK and Dutch trade data, among others. Flags: chinese_soe_adjacent, soe_adjacent, Xinjiang product-blueprint sub-tier.
calls.interpretation: The record ties the Jakarta office to the Morowali site. The profile did not list partner names.

calls.question: Who owns the plant, per Sayari?
calls.result_summary: 2 beneficial owners, both from Indonesian UBO data: Chen Xuehua (Tongxiang, Zhejiang address; owner ID 771950) and a second individual (Taipei address; name withheld because no role is explained). No company shareholders, no percentages.
calls.interpretation: A Chinese individual from Huayou's home city is a registered beneficial owner, but no corporate chain is shown.

calls.question: Which record is the Chinese parent?
calls.result_summary: 13 records. Main: Zhejiang Huayou Cobalt Co., Ltd. (GstlFKZ-29D5gm8p3Xg6mw), LEI 30030099QFLNMEGP7M05, credit code 913300007368873961, flags incl. regulatory_action. A Chinese-name record (WsTfWkdMP4iuUyQG7iidlQ) holds organisation code 736887396 and owned_by_chinese_soe flags. Others are trade-name fragments in the UK, Italy and Singapore.
calls.interpretation: The parent resolves on an LEI. The two main records share an organisation code.

calls.question: Is the plant linked to Huayou in Sayari?
calls.result_summary: Path of length 3: the plant receives from Zhejiang Huayou Import & Export, which has Huayou Cobalt as shareholder.
calls.interpretation: The shortest link is trade, not ownership, as with BTR in Case 1.

calls.question: Does Sayari link the beneficial owner Chen Xuehua to Huayou?
calls.result_summary: Path of length 4 runs through the plant and Huayou Import & Export; no direct shareholding from Chen Xuehua to Huayou.
calls.interpretation: Sayari does not hold Chen Xuehua's Huayou stake; that comes from open sources.

params.query: PT Huayue Nickel Cobalt shareholding Huayou Tsingshan Morowali HPAL MHP

calls.question: Who owns HNC and what does it make?
calls.result_summary: Nickel Industries' Nov 2023 EGM notice: it bought 10% of HNC from a Tsingshan entity for US$270m; other shareholders Huayou (57%) and CMOC (30%). AEER (Feb 2025): Huayou 57%, CMOC 30%, Nickel Industries 10%, Huaqing Hualong Consulting 2%, Long Sincere 1%; HNC capacity 60,000 t/y MHP; Chen Xuehua 6.43% of Huayou. MBMA press release: commissioned Nov 2021, nameplate by Apr 2022. Nickel Industries site: 4 autoclaves, 60 kt Ni in MHP.
calls.interpretation: Ownership is well documented in open sources: a Chinese parent with a clear majority.

calls.question: Who does the plant ship to?
calls.result_summary: 50 of 53 partners on page 1: Huayou companies (Guangxi, Quzhou, Hong Kong), CMOC (5 records), CNGR (2), IXM, Trafigura, Mercuria, Brunp, Wanhua, Umicore's Jiangmen JV, traders and logistics firms, and US valve makers ValvTechnologies and Caldera Engineering. No Korean or Japanese cathode maker, no US cell plant.
calls.interpretation: Almost every buyer is Chinese, a Chinese-group company or a commodity trader.

calls.question: Who are the remaining buyers?
calls.result_summary: 3 more: Mercuria Energy Trading SA, Tongxiang Huaang Trading (a Tongxiang trader with owned_by_chinese_soe flags) and Jinchuan Group Nickel Salts.
calls.interpretation: All 53 partners seen; none is a US battery maker.

calls.question: What does the plant export, and where to?
calls.result_summary: 382 rows, all with this plant as supplier. HS 7501.20 (nickel intermediate products) 308; valves (8481.80) 45; others small. Arrivals: China 293, USA 48, Hong Kong 14, Switzerland 8, Singapore 7, Australia 4, India 3. Dates 12 Mar 2021 – 29 Aug 2026.
calls.interpretation: MHP is the main export and China the main destination. The 48 US rows need checking.

calls.question: Does any nickel go straight to the US?
calls.result_summary: All 48 US rows are valves and valve parts with serial numbers: ValvTechnologies (26 + 2 rows) and Caldera Engineering (20), Jan 2023 – Nov 2025. One row is coded HS 8103.20 (a tantalum valve). No nickel product.
calls.interpretation: No direct US nickel flows. The rows fit equipment going back to its makers.

calls.question: Who buys the plant's MHP (HS 7501.20)?
calls.result_summary: 100 of 308 rows, Aug 2025 – Aug 2026, 25 buyer pairs. Top: Guangxi Huayou New Material 27, IXM Shanghai (two records) 23, Quzhou Huayou 10, CNMC International Trading 8. Also CNGR (2 companies), Brunp, Jinchuan, Umicore's Jiangmen JV, Trafigura, Mercuria and others.
calls.interpretation: The newest rows go mostly to Huayou's own Chinese plants and to traders.

calls.question: Who bought MHP earlier?
calls.result_summary: Rows 101–200, Aug 2024 – Aug 2025. Huayou (Hong Kong) 20, CMOC Limited 18 + 2, IXM 16 + 1, Tsing Creation 15, Quzhou Huayou 11, Guangxi Huayou 7, Malco Energy (India) 3, plus single rows to Wanhua, Weiming, Jinchuan and others. The last 108 rows (to Aug 2024) were not read.

params.query: prohibited foreign entity rules 45X Indonesian nickel Chinese-owned smelters battery supply chain 2026

calls.question: How do the PFE rules treat a Chinese-owned supplier?
calls.result_summary: Tax Law Center: OBBBA PFE entity, payment and material-assistance rules apply to 45X components sold in tax years after 2025. Certainty Software summary: a foreign-influenced entity includes one where a single specified foreign entity owns more than 25%; material-assistance thresholds for 45X battery components rise to 85% by 2030. Tax Law Center also cites IRS Notice 2026-15 on supplier certifications.
calls.interpretation: Under these tests, a supplier majority-owned by a Chinese company warrants due diligence before its material counts toward a 45X claim.

params.query: Huayou POSCO Future M precursor supply joint venture nickel Indonesia

calls.question: Did Huayou supply POSCO with precursor, and does it still?
calls.result_summary: Huayou's 2023 annual report: a long-term ternary precursor supply agreement with POSCO Chemical, and an MOU with LG Chem on precursor and cathode. Korea Times (Jun 2025): POSCO Future M scrapped its Huayou precursor JV (Sep 2024), bought out Huayou's share of POSCO HY Clean Metal, and plans China-free precursor in Gwangyang because Chinese-made precursors lost US credit eligibility. KED Global (May 2023) on the planned JV.
calls.interpretation: Corroborates the Huayou-to-POSCO precursor rows, and explains why they stop after 2023.

params.query: Indonesia nickel FEOC 30D clean vehicle credit Chinese ownership 25% Indonesia free trade agreement critical minerals deal

calls.question: How has the US treated Indonesian nickel?
calls.result_summary: Fastmarkets: Treasury's Dec 2023 FEOC definition (25% Chinese ownership) leaves most Indonesian nickel, including Huayou, Tsingshan, CNGR and Lygend projects, outside 30D credits; exceptions are Antam, most Vale Indonesia operations and an Eramet–BASF plan. Globaldeal.io: Pomalaa (Vale, Sumitomo Metal Mining, Ford) is presented as the non-FEOC template.
calls.interpretation: Chinese-majority plants like HNC were already outside the EV credit; the 2026 PFE rules extend the ownership test to manufacturing credits.
